articles.title: Los Angeles Chargers vs New York Jets Week 11: Couldn't Get a Stop, 24-27
articles.matchup: Final: New York Jets (3-8) 27, Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 24, Sun., Nov. 22, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: vs New England Patriots, Sun., Nov. 29, 4:05 PM ET, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood
articles.text:
Six Jets possessions, five Jets scores, and one more home loss for the Los Angeles Chargers, 27-24 to the New York Jets at SoFi Stadium. On Saturday, the 20th Great Los Angeles Walk set off down the full length of Wilshire Boulevard from Pershing Square to the beach, and on Sunday the Jets strolled up and down our field like they'd signed up for it. We're 1-9, and 0-5 at home.

New York never punted. Not once. They went nine of 11 on third downs, and Geno Smith completed 17 of 21. We couldn't get off the field, and that's the whole story of the afternoon.

It stings because we fought. Down 17-3 in the second quarter, Justin Herbert drove us 72 yards in 12 plays and ran it in himself from 10 yards out on the last play of the half. 17-10. After their 18-play field goal drive made it 20-10, Herbert hit Ladd McConkey from 11 yards early in the fourth, and it was a three-point game.

McConkey caught both of Herbert's touchdowns and five balls on the day. Omarion Hampton ran 14 times for 89 yards, including a 36-yarder. Herbert finished 15 of 21 for 131 yards with no interceptions and ran for 32 more. But he got sacked six times, and that's a lot of drives going backward.

Down 27-17, we put together a 16-play, 63-yard march that took 7:48, with a challenge that flipped an incomplete throw to McConkey into a catch along the way, and Herbert found him from 6 yards out with 1:58 left. 27-24. We still had three timeouts. We used all of them, and the Jets ran out the clock anyway.

Cameron Dicker drilled a 52-yard field goal in the first quarter. Elijah Molden made eight tackles, Cam Hart had six, and Troy Dye got our only sack. We didn't cough the ball up once, and we still lost, because a defense has to force a punt at some point.

The New England Patriots come to SoFi Stadium next Sunday, Nov. 29, at 4:05 PM ET. One home win. That's all I'm asking for before Christmas. Bolt up.

articles.title: New York Jets vs Los Angeles Chargers Week 11: No Punts, No Problem, 27-24
articles.matchup: Final: New York Jets (3-8) 27, Los Angeles Chargers (1-9) 24, Sun., Nov. 22, SoFi Stadium, Inglewood. Next: at Miami Dolphins, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
The New York Jets won 27-24 in Inglewood without punting once, and the Los Angeles Chargers never figured out how to get the ball back from us. Sunday was the 250th anniversary of George Washington's Retreat to Victory at Historic New Bridge Landing in Bergen County, with reenactors leading his troops back across the bridge, and out at SoFi our guys did the opposite of retreating. We're 3-8, and the five-game losing streak is history.

Geno Smith was surgical. He went 17 of 21 for 176 yards and three touchdowns with no interceptions, and we converted nine of 11 third downs. Sterling Shepard caught two balls all day and both were touchdowns, from 8 and 16 yards. Breece Hall caught a 7-yard score in the second quarter and ran 20 times for 86 yards.

We had the ball six times and scored on five of them. The one I'll tell my grandkids about went 18 plays and took exactly 10 minutes off the third-quarter clock. Braelon Allen carried it six times on that march alone, and Jason Sanders finished it with a 24-yard field goal for a 20-10 lead. Allen ended up with 75 yards on 16 carries, and Sanders also hit from 50.

Justin Herbert answered with a touchdown throw to Ladd McConkey early in the fourth, 20-17, and Geno came right back with a six-play, 62-yard drive that ended with Shepard's 16-yard catch. 27-17.

The defense bent, but it got home six times. David Bailey had two sacks and knocked the ball loose once, Jowon Briggs had a sack and a half, Harrison Phillips had one, and Jamien Sherwood made 11 tackles. Herbert still found McConkey again from 6 yards out with 1:58 left, and it was 27-24, and my stomach dropped.

Then Hall and Allen slammed the door. Hall carried four straight times after the kickoff, the Chargers burned all three timeouts, and Allen ripped off 15 yards on the last snap. No turnovers, four penalties, and a punter who never got his uniform dirty. That's how you win on the road.

Next Sunday, Nov. 29, we visit the Miami Dolphins at Hard Rock Stadium at 1:00 PM ET. J-E-T-S, Jets, Jets, Jets!

articles.title: Carolina Panthers vs Baltimore Ravens Week 11: Fitzgerald From 37, Dodson Seals It, 35-33
articles.matchup: Final: Carolina Panthers (5-5) 35, Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 33, Sun., Nov. 22, Bank of America Stadium, Charlotte. Next: at Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Mon., Nov. 30, 8:15 PM ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
Heart-attack football in Charlotte: the Carolina Panthers outlasted the Baltimore Ravens 35-33 on Sunday. It was our Salute to Service game, and before kickoff an Apache battalion from the North Carolina Army National Guard that calls itself the Panthers flew above Bank of America Stadium. Our Panthers had to claw for every inch after that, and we're 5-5.

It began ugly. Bryce Young got sacked in our own end zone for a safety, Jacoby Brissett hit Rashod Bateman for a 52-yard touchdown, and we were down 9-0 before I'd found my seat.

Then Young went to work. He hit Mitchell Evans for a 23-yard touchdown with one second left in the first quarter. Brycen Tremayne jumped on a muffed punt at the Baltimore 23, and Chuba Hubbard ran 18 yards for a 14-12 lead two plays later. Devontez Walker took the next kickoff 86 yards for a Baltimore score, and we answered right back: Young to Tetairoa McMillan from 7 yards out, then Hubbard ran in the two-point try for a 22-19 lead.

Hubbard was a bulldozer all day, with 27 carries, 120 yards and two touchdowns, including a 1-yarder that made it 29-26 in the third. Young finished 22 of 30 for 254 yards and two scores with one interception. McMillan caught six for 71.

Our defense kept taking the ball away. Will Lee III punched it loose from Justice Hill at our 1, and it rolled out of the end zone for a touchback. Early in the fourth, our challenge turned an incomplete throw to Derrick Henry into a catch and a fumble, and Tyrel Dodson came up with it.

Henry still got us, scoring from 15 yards with 6:32 left, and Baltimore led 33-32. I didn't breathe for five minutes. Young answered with a 12-play drive, Tommy Tremble made an 18-yard grab, and Ryan Fitzgerald drilled a 37-yarder with 1:44 left. 35-33.

Then Dodson finished it. Brissett threw for Bateman with 36 seconds left, and Dodson intercepted it at the Baltimore 44. Two kneels later, the place exploded. Princely Umanmielen added a sack and a half, and Dodson finished with eight tackles to go with his two takeaways.

Next up is Monday night at Raymond James Stadium against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, Monday, Nov. 30, at 8:15 PM ET. The Bucs beat us in October, and we owe them one. Let's roll, Carolina.

articles.title: Baltimore Ravens vs Carolina Panthers Week 11: Four Giveaways Sink Us, 33-35
articles.matchup: Final: Carolina Panthers (5-5) 35, Baltimore Ravens (4-7) 33, Sun., Nov. 22, Bank of America Stadium, Charlotte. Next: at Houston Texans, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Reliant Stadium, Houston
articles.text:
Four turnovers and a two-point loss: that's the Baltimore Ravens' Sunday in Charlotte, beaten 35-33 by the Carolina Panthers. Back home, the German Christmas Village was open at the Inner Harbor all weekend with folks hunting for holiday gifts, and down in Carolina we were handing out presents of our own. We're 4-7, and that's six losses in a row.

What makes me want to throw the remote is that this team can play. We were up 9-0 less than four minutes in. Mike Green sacked Bryce Young in the end zone for a safety, and on our next possession Jacoby Brissett dropped a 52-yard touchdown into Rashod Bateman's hands. Three plays, 70 yards, done.

Devontez Walker was electric. He took a kickoff 86 yards to the house in the second quarter, racked up 211 return yards on seven kickoffs, and caught a 34-yard throw. Derrick Henry ran 13 times for 94 yards. Justice Hill had 69 yards on six carries and a 19-yard touchdown run. Zay Flowers caught eight balls for 97.

And then the giveaways. LaJohntay Wester muffed a punt that Carolina grabbed at our 23, and two plays later Chuba Hubbard ran it in. Hill broke a 36-yard run down to their 1, had the ball knocked loose, and it bounced out of the end zone for a touchback. That's seven points gone. Early in the fourth, Carolina challenged a throw to Henry that was ruled incomplete, won it, and the catch became a fumble.

Henry still put us ahead, scoring from 15 yards out with 6:32 left to make it 33-32. Then our defense let them go 55 yards in 12 plays, and Ryan Fitzgerald kicked a 37-yarder with 1:44 left. 35-33. Brissett had time to set up a winner, but his throw for Bateman got intercepted by Tyrel Dodson at our 44 with 36 seconds to go.

Brissett finished 24 of 37 for 276 yards. We gained 421 yards to their 378 and averaged 7.1 yards a carry. Trenton Simpson made 10 tackles, Roquan Smith had nine, and Green finished with two sacks. You don't lose that game unless you give the ball away, and we gave it away four times.

Next Sunday, Nov. 29, we visit the Houston Texans at 1:00 PM ET. One request, fellas: hold onto the football. That's the whole list.

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles vs Pittsburgh Steelers Week 11: Skid Snapped, 19-16
articles.matchup: Final: Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 19, Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) 16, Sun., Nov. 22, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia. Next: at Dallas Cowboys, Thu., Nov. 26, 4:30 PM ET, AT&T Stadium, Arlington
articles.text:
Seven straight losses, gone: the Philadelphia Eagles beat the Pittsburgh Steelers 19-16 at the Linc on Sunday. It was 60 degrees in Center City on Saturday, folks were walking around the Christmas Village preview weekend at LOVE Park in T-shirts, and now the whole city finally feels warm again. We're 3-7, and I can breathe.

Jake Elliott is the man today. Four field goals, four makes, from 41, 29, 53 and 55 yards. The 55-yarder came with 4:19 left and pushed us up 19-9, and we needed every bit of it, because Pittsburgh scored a touchdown with 1:21 to go.

Saquon Barkley gave us the only touchdown, a 38-yard run around the left end with 35 seconds left in the first quarter, and the Linc shook. He finished with 75 yards on 17 carries. We were up 13-0 after one quarter, helped by a fourth-down stop on Pittsburgh's opening drive at their own 40.

Then the offense went quiet, and I won't pretend it didn't. Joe Milton went 11 of 21 for 141 yards and got sacked three times, and we had 214 yards. We coughed up the second-half kickoff when Jaydon Blue fumbled, and the Steelers turned that into a field goal. Dallas Goedert's 38-yard catch in the first quarter and Darius Cooper's four grabs for 59 were about all we had through the air, along with five catches from DeVonta Smith.

The defense won this game, plain and simple. Pittsburgh ran 69 plays and got 255 yards out of them. Aaron Rodgers went down five times: Byron Young had two sacks, and Nolan Smith Jr., Jonathan Greenard and Gabe Hall had one each. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. made 13 tackles and Jonathan Jones broke up three throws. The Steelers got inside our 20 twice and left with zero touchdowns.

Braden Mann boomed four punts at 59.3 yards apiece, which is ridiculous, and we drew only four flags.

The last 1:21 was Will Shipley running twice, a 7-yard catch by Smith to move the chains, and Milton kneeling it out. I have never enjoyed a kneel-down more in my life.

Now the short week and a big one: we visit the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington on Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 4:30 PM ET. Hand me the stuffing. Fly, Eagles, fly.

articles.title: Pittsburgh Steelers vs Philadelphia Eagles Week 11: Boswell Can't Do It All, 16-19
articles.matchup: Final: Philadelphia Eagles (3-7) 19, Pittsburgh Steelers (6-4) 16, Sun., Nov. 22, Lincoln Financial Field, Philadelphia. Next: vs Denver Broncos, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:00 PM ET, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh
articles.text:
Zambelli fireworks lit up the Allegheny on Saturday night, and on Sunday the Pittsburgh Steelers fizzled in South Philly, losing 19-16 to the Philadelphia Eagles. Light Up Night turned 65 this year and the Rachel Carson Bridge threw itself a 100th birthday party Downtown, but our offense stayed dark until the last five minutes. We're 6-4 with two straight losses, and I'm steaming.

We dug a 13-0 hole in the first quarter. Our opening drive died on fourth down at our own 40, which handed Philly a short field and a Jake Elliott field goal. He added another one, and then Saquon Barkley went 38 yards around the left end for a touchdown with 35 seconds left in the quarter.

Give the defense its due, because it kept us alive. Philadelphia finished with 214 yards. Alex Highsmith had two sacks, Jack Sawyer had one, Cameron Heyward broke up a throw, and Patrick Queen made a tackle for loss. Robert Spears-Jennings punched the ball loose on the second-half kickoff, Carson Bruener grabbed it at their 26, and that turned into three points.

Chris Boswell was perfect from 25, 40 and 52 yards. But you don't beat anybody living on field goals. We got inside their 20 twice and came out with zero touchdowns, converted five of 17 third downs, and Aaron Rodgers went down five times. Philly's kicker hit from 53 and 55 in the second half, and that 55-yarder with 4:19 left made it 19-9.

Then, finally, the offense showed up. Rodgers led a 13-play, 72-yard drive with a couple of scrambles to keep it moving and dropped a 20-yard touchdown deep left to Max Hurleman with 1:21 left. 19-16. We needed one stop after that and didn't get it. DeVonta Smith caught a 7-yard throw to move the chains, and Philly knelt out the clock.

Rodgers finished 30 of 44 for 227 yards. Hurleman was the bright spot with six catches for 61 yards and the touchdown, plus 68 yards on kick and punt returns. Pat Freiermuth caught five for 39, Roman Wilson had a 33-yard grab, and Cameron Johnston averaged 49.2 yards on six punts. We held the ball for 35:30 and still lost.

That one hurts, because a team that sacks the other quarterback three times and wins the turnover battle should walk out of there with a win.

Next up is Black Friday football at Acrisure Stadium against the Denver Broncos, Friday, Nov. 27, at 3:00 PM ET. Turkey sandwiches in the bag, Terrible Towels in the air. Let's get the taste of this one out of our mouths.

articles.title: Kansas City Chiefs vs Arizona Cardinals Week 11: Kelce Twice, Easy Sunday, 34-7
articles.matchup: Final: Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 34, Arizona Cardinals (3-8) 7, Sun., Nov. 22, Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City. Next: at Buffalo Bills, Thu., Nov. 26, 8:20 PM ET, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park
articles.text:
Arrowhead got an easy one Sunday: Kansas City Chiefs 34, Arizona Cardinals 7. Half this town spent the weekend strolling Holiday Swing at Union Station, the 16th year of that open-air market of handmade KC goods, and Patrick Mahomes spent his afternoon shopping for open receivers in the Arizona secondary. We're 8-2, and that's three wins in a row.

Mahomes was surgical: 27 of 39, 324 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions. Travis Kelce caught two of them, an 8-yarder to finish the opening drive and a 22-yarder with 1:54 left in the half, and ended the day with six catches for 74 yards. Number 87 still finds the soft spot in a zone like somebody drew him a map.

Emmett Johnson did the dirty work. He carried 23 times for 105 yards, and his 3-yard touchdown capped a 16-play, 80-yard grind that ate 7:22 and made it 14-0 with 48 seconds left in the first quarter. Josh Downs caught four for 59 and Rashee Rice caught six for 53.

The drive I'll be bragging about at Thanksgiving began at our own 3 late in the third quarter. Ninety-seven yards in nine plays, with Cyrus Allen hauling in a 26-yarder, and Mahomes hit Xavier Worthy for an 18-yard touchdown on the first snap of the fourth. 34-7. Good night, Arizona.

Harrison Butker hit from 40 and 44, the second one as time ran out in the half, so we went to the locker room up 27-7. Matt Araiza boomed three punts at 53.3 yards a pop.

Then there's George Karlaftis. Two and a half sacks, two tackles for loss, five quarterback hits and a strip-sack in the third quarter, though Arizona got lucky and fell on the ball. Drue Tranquill led us with eight tackles. Their lone score was a 2-yard throw in the second quarter, and they never scored again. They went nowhere on both fourth-down tries and managed 205 yards.

No turnovers for either side, and we drew two flags for 15 yards all day. That's a grown-up football team.

Now the short week: we visit the Buffalo Bills at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park on Thanksgiving night, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 PM ET. Save me a plate of burnt ends, Mom. I'll eat at halftime.

articles.title: Arizona Cardinals vs Kansas City Chiefs Week 11: Buried at Arrowhead, 7-34
articles.matchup: Final: Kansas City Chiefs (8-2) 34, Arizona Cardinals (3-8) 7, Sun., Nov. 22, Arrowhead Stadium, Kansas City. Next: vs Washington Commanders, Sun., Nov. 29, 4:25 PM ET, State Farm Stadium, Glendale
articles.text:
The Arizona Cardinals went to Arrowhead on Sunday and got buried 34-7 by the Kansas City Chiefs. Back home, the 30th Hidden in the Hills art tour had studios open all weekend in Cave Creek, Carefree and North Scottsdale, and I'd have rather spent the afternoon looking at a painting of a saguaro. We're 3-8, and that's three losses in a row.

It got away from us early. Kansas City scored on its first two drives, an 8-yard touchdown catch by Travis Kelce and a 3-yard Emmett Johnson run, and that second march went 16 plays and 80 yards and kept our defense on the field for 7:22. It was 14-0 after one quarter, and the noise in that place doesn't help a road offense hear the snap count.

We did punch back once. Josh Johnson took us 63 yards in 10 plays and found Simi Fehoko from 2 yards out, and it was 14-7 in the second quarter. For about five minutes I believed. Then Harrison Butker kicked a 40-yarder, Kelce caught a 22-yard score, Butker hit from 44 as the half ran out, and we were down 27-7 at the break.

Johnson finished 18 of 31 for 155 yards with no interceptions, and we didn't lose a fumble, so at least we didn't gift them a short field. What we couldn't do was keep George Karlaftis out of the backfield. He had two and a half sacks and five hits on our quarterback, and one of those sacks knocked the ball loose before Josh Fryar dove on it.

Trey McBride fought for nine catches and 54 yards on 14 targets. Harrison Wallace III caught four for 57, with a long of 25. Bam Knight ran seven times for 35. Jack Gibbens made 10 tackles, Mack Wilson Sr. had eight and Budda Baker had six. Max Melton brought back three kickoffs for 103 yards, which gave us decent field position we mostly wasted.

We came up empty on both fourth-down tries, including an 11-play fourth-quarter drive that died on downs, and we never scored after halftime. Kansas City, meanwhile, went 97 yards from its own 3 and finished it with an 18-yard Xavier Worthy touchdown on the first snap of the fourth quarter. We had 205 yards for the whole game. That's not enough to beat anybody.

Next Sunday, Nov. 29, we're back home at State Farm Stadium in Glendale against the Washington Commanders at 4:25 PM ET. Our own building, our own crowd, and a desperate need to remember what a touchdown in the second half feels like. Bird Gang, show up loud.

articles.title: San Francisco 49ers vs Minnesota Vikings Week 11: Purdy Owns Mexico City, 35-10
articles.matchup: Final: San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 35, Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 10, Sun., Nov. 22, Estadio Banorte, Mexico City. Next: vs Seattle Seahawks, Sun., Nov. 29, 4:25 PM ET, Levi's Stadium, Santa Clara
articles.text:
49ers 35, Vikings 10, and Mexico City just got a Faithful education. We're 9-1, we've won three straight, and Brock Purdy threw like the altitude was a rumor: 21 of 26 for 255 yards, three touchdowns, no interceptions.

The NFL hadn't played in Mexico City in four years, every seat at Estadio Banorte was gone, and 85,612 people showed up for our "home" game.

George Kittle got us rolling with a 17-yard touchdown catch on the opening drive, then caught an 8-yarder early in the second quarter. Mike Evans ran the show from there: six catches, 109 yards, gains of 34 and 29, and a 4-yard touchdown with 2:09 left in the half to make it 21-10.

Then came the 10 seconds I'll be telling people about for years. On Minnesota's very next snap, Ji'Ayir Brown jumped a throw in the middle of the field and took it 18 yards for a touchdown. 28-10 at the half. Ballgame, basically.

Our defense owned the second half. Deommodore Lenoir punched the ball out of Justin Jefferson's hands after a 25-yard catch and came up with it himself. The Vikings got deep twice in the fourth and came away empty both times on fourth down, once on a 10-yard catch on fourth-and-13 and once on an incompletion. Renardo Green had nine tackles, Fred Warner had eight, and DeForest Buckner and Osa Odighizuwa split a sack. Minnesota did not score after the second quarter.

And the best drive of the year: the Vikings pinned us at our own 2 with a big punt, and we went 98 yards in 13 plays. Christian McCaffrey finished it with a 6-yard run early in the fourth. Four trips inside the 20, four touchdowns. Zero turnovers.

Even the weird stuff went our way. After our punt with 11 seconds left in the half, the Vikings tried a 71-yard fair-catch free kick. Came up short. You don't see that one every year, and I'll take the free entertainment.

Next up, Seattle comes to Levi's Stadium on Nov. 29. Division game, back in Santa Clara. Bring it.

articles.title: Minnesota Vikings vs San Francisco 49ers Week 11: Mexico City Meltdown, 10-35
articles.matchup: Final: San Francisco 49ers (9-1) 35, Minnesota Vikings (7-3) 10, Sun., Nov. 22, Estadio Banorte, Mexico City. Next: vs Atlanta Falcons, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, U.S. Bank Stadium, Minneapolis
articles.text:
49ers 35, Vikings 10, and our first trip to Mexico City ended with my head in my hands. We're 7-3 and we've lost three of our last four. No time to sulk, either.

Back home Friday night, Viking Lakes in Eagan switched on Magic of Lights for Winter SKOLstice, a drive-through light show in our team's own backyard. Those lights were the brightest part of our weekend.

It wasn't awful early. San Francisco scored on its opening drive, and we answered with a 9-play, 90-yard march that Aaron Jones finished with an 11-yard touchdown run around the left end. 7-7. Will Reichard added a 48-yarder in the second quarter, and it was 14-10. I was feeling fine.

Then the floor caved in. Brock Purdy hit Mike Evans for a touchdown with 2:09 left in the half, and on our very next play Kirk Cousins threw one right to Ji'Ayir Brown, who ran it back 18 yards for a score. Two touchdowns in 10 seconds. 28-10 at the half. You can't hand a team like that free points.

The third quarter didn't help. Justin Jefferson made a 25-yard catch and Deommodore Lenoir ripped the ball out. Then Brett Thorson boomed a 57-yard punt that pinned them at their own 2, and they went 98 yards anyway, with Christian McCaffrey scoring from 6.

Cousins went 26 of 38 for 235 yards. Jefferson caught seven balls for 86 yards, T.J. Hockenson had six for 55, and Tai Felton had six for 42. On defense, Blake Cashman and James Pierre each made nine tackles, Eric Wilson got the only sack, and Jalen Redmond had two tackles for loss. We also missed from 55, came up short on a 71-yard fair-catch free kick, and went 1 for 3 on fourth down.

Purdy only threw five incompletions all night. We have to get after the quarterback better than that.

Atlanta comes to U.S. Bank Stadium on Nov. 29. Back indoors, back home, and we'd better be loud. Skol.

articles.title: Detroit Lions vs Tampa Bay Buccaneers Week 11: Gibbs Twice, 31-21
articles.matchup: Final: Detroit Lions (8-2) 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 21, Sun., Nov. 22, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: vs Chicago Bears, Thu., Nov. 26, 1:00 PM ET, Ford Field, Detroit
articles.text:
Lions 31, Buccaneers 21 at Ford Field, and nobody has beaten us at home yet. Six and oh in our building, 8-2 overall, and Jahmyr Gibbs slammed the door with two fourth-quarter touchdowns.

This one was tighter than I wanted. Tampa Bay chewed up eight minutes on its second drive, and our defense stuffed Bucky Irving on fourth-and-1 at our 9. Then we went 90 yards in 14 plays, and Jared Goff hit Amon-Ra St. Brown for a 14-yard touchdown.

Goff was sharp all day, 20 of 28 for 279 yards and two touchdowns. The best throw of the day was a 57-yarder to Jameson Williams down the middle in the third that made it 17-7. Sam LaPorta caught a 47-yarder on our first drive, and Brock Wright had a 27-yard grab that set up Jake Bates from 56 right before the half. Bates missed from 53 early, but that 56-yarder made it 10-0.

Then the Bucs hung around. Baker Mayfield found Ted Hurst III for a 23-yard score with four seconds left in the half, and Irving punched one in from the 1 late in the third. 17-14. My stomach was in knots.

That's when Gibbs grabbed this game by the collar. After we traded punts, he capped a 59-yard drive with a 1-yard run to make it 24-14. Then the defense sacked Mayfield on third down and again on fourth, Trevor Nowaske first, then Derrick Moore and Malcolm Rodriguez together. Gibbs ripped off 26 yards on the next drive and scored from the 4. 31-14 with 1:55 left. Ballgame. He finished with 98 yards on 23 carries.

The defense deserves a shout. Four sacks, with Chuck Clark and DJ Wonnum getting one each, and Rock Ya-Sin made 10 tackles. Brian Branch broke up two throws. Hurst caught a second touchdown with eight seconds left, but by then the place was already rocking.

Downtown had its own glow on Saturday night. Light Up Beacon Park lit a 20-foot Michigan-grown tree with more than 125,000 lights around the park, plus live reindeer and a visit from Santa. Michigan trees and Michigan football, both lit up this weekend.

Now the big one. The Chicago Bears come to Ford Field on Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 PM ET, with both of us at 8-2. Turkey first, then a division fight. One Pride.

articles.matchup: Final: Detroit Lions (8-2) 31, Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-7) 21, Sun., Nov. 22, Ford Field, Detroit. Next: vs Carolina Panthers, Mon., Nov. 30, 8:15 PM ET, Raymond James Stadium, Tampa
articles.text:
Detroit 31, Tampa Bay 21, and for three quarters at Ford Field we were right there. Down 17-14 heading into the fourth, in a building where the Lions hadn't lost all year, with our offense moving. Then Jahmyr Gibbs happened, and now we're 3-7.

Our second drive is the one I'll replay all week. Twelve plays, 47 yards, eight minutes off the clock, and Bucky Irving got stopped for a 1-yard loss on fourth-and-1 at the Detroit 9. Points there change the whole afternoon. We went 0 for 2 on fourth down, and both of them hurt.

Baker Mayfield played tough. He was 20 of 33 for 187 yards with two touchdowns and no interceptions, and he ran six times for 36 yards. Ted Hurst III was the bright spot, five catches for 56 yards and both scores, a 23-yarder with four seconds left in the half and a 4-yarder with eight seconds left in the game. Irving ran 18 times for 68 yards, ripped off a 23-yard run late in the third and finished that drive with a 1-yard touchdown.

But the defense couldn't get off the field when it counted. Jared Goff threw for 279 yards. Jameson Williams got behind us for a 57-yard touchdown. Gibbs scored twice in the fourth. Josiah Trotter made 14 tackles, Tykee Smith had nine, and David Walker got to Goff once. One sack all day. That won't do.

And when we needed a drive at 24-14, Mayfield got sacked on third down and again on fourth, and the Lions needed 1:21 to make it 31-14. Hurst's second touchdown made the final look closer than the fourth quarter felt.

Back home, Winter Village opened Friday at Curtis Hixon Waterfront Park along the Riverwalk, with ice skating right in downtown Tampa. Ice in Tampa? Fine by me. Our defensive front looked frozen all afternoon in Detroit, so I guess it fits the week.

Cowboys 51, Titans 30, and Dak Prescott was about as close to perfect as it gets at AT&T Stadium. Twenty-eight of 33. Three hundred twenty-five yards. Four touchdown throws, plus a 2-yard run of his own. We're 5-6 and alive again.

Every time we got close, we finished. Six trips inside the Titans' 20, six touchdowns. No sacks allowed, no turnovers, 480 yards. That's what this offense is supposed to look like every week.

CeeDee Lamb was a problem all day, 11 catches for 132 yards and an 8-yard touchdown. George Pickens added seven for 102 and a 10-yard score, plus a 30-yard grab that got us to the 2 in the third. Javonte Williams ran one in and caught an 11-yard touchdown. KaVontae Turpin took a handoff 22 yards to the house in the first quarter, and James Mitchell caught two for 40.

Tennessee hung around for a while, and I'll give Cam Ward credit. He snuck in a 1-yarder and hit Carnell Tate for 59 yards, and in the third it was 34-23. Then Dak took us 74 yards in six plays and scored himself from the 2. 41-23. Goodnight.

The defense had its moments too. Quinnen Williams had two sacks and three tackles for loss, and his strip-sack in the fourth was the play of the day. Markquese Bell scooped the ball at our 15 and ran it 70 yards to their 15, and three plays later Dak hit Brevyn Spann-Ford for a 2-yard touchdown. James Houston had two sacks of his own. Justin Barron led us with nine tackles.

Now the gripe. Eleven penalties for 128 yards. We can't hand out free yards like that on Thursday.

Arlington had a festive weekend all around. The 16th annual Texas Christkindl Market opened Friday on the North Plaza of Globe Life Field, right next door, free to get in, with fake snow falling almost every day. Fake snow in Arlington I can believe. Fifty-one points? I checked the scoreboard twice.

No time to sit around. The Philadelphia Eagles come to AT&T Stadium on Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 4:30 PM ET. Bring the same Dak. How 'bout them Cowboys.

articles.title: Tennessee Titans vs Dallas Cowboys Week 11: 30 Points Wasted, 30-51
articles.matchup: Final: Dallas Cowboys (5-6) 51, Tennessee Titans (1-9) 30, Sun., Nov. 22, AT&T Stadium, Arlington. Next: at Jacksonville Jaguars, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, EverBank Stadium, Jacksonville
articles.text:
Dallas 51, Tennessee 30. We put up 30 points on the road and lost by 21, which tells you all you need to know about how our defense spent Sunday in Arlington. We're 1-9.

Cam Ward did his part. He went 21 of 30 for 248 yards with two touchdown throws and no interceptions, and he snuck one in from a yard out. His 59-yard strike to Carnell Tate in the third quarter cut it to 34-23 and had me off the couch. Tony Pollard ran 21 times for 110 yards and looked like the toughest guy on the field.

Calvin Ridley caught five for 68, and his 12-yard touchdown with 31 seconds left came on fourth-and-8, the second fourth-and-8 we converted on that drive. Chimere Dike caught six for 69 and returned six kickoffs for 127 yards. Joey Slye hit all three field goals, from 38, 48 and 28. The offense moved the ball. That's not where this one went wrong.

Here's where it went wrong. Dak Prescott went 28 of 33 for 325 yards and four touchdowns, and nobody laid a hand on him. Zero sacks. Dallas went 6 for 6 in the red zone. CeeDee Lamb caught 11 balls, George Pickens caught seven, and every time we scored in the third quarter, they answered right back.

And the one time we had a real chance to make it a game in the fourth, Ward got stripped by Quinnen Williams at the Dallas 20, and the Cowboys ran it all the way back to our 15. They scored three plays later. Ward got sacked five times on the day. Joshua Williams made 11 tackles and Cedric Gray had eight, but we never took the ball away once.

Back home, Cheekwood's Holiday LIGHTS opened Friday, more than a million lights along a one-mile walking path through the gardens. I'm heading out there this week. After three hours of watching our secondary chase Dallas receivers, a long, quiet walk in Nashville sounds like exactly what the doctor ordered.

Next: the Titans head to EverBank Stadium to face the Jacksonville Jaguars, Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 PM ET. Keep Cam Ward upright, keep feeding Pollard, and find somebody who can get to the quarterback. Titan Up.

articles.title: Chicago Bears vs New Orleans Saints Week 11: Safety First, 21-13
articles.matchup: Final: Chicago Bears (8-2) 21, New Orleans Saints (3-7) 13, Sun., Nov. 22, Soldier Field, Chicago. Next: at Detroit Lions, Thu., Nov. 26, 1:00 PM ET, Ford Field, Detroit
articles.text:
Bears 21, Saints 13 at Soldier Field, and we're 8-2. Eight and two! Write it on the fridge. Then scribble a note next to it about the defense, because that's who won this one.

Caleb Williams was sharp when it counted, 15 of 23 for 181 yards and two touchdowns. After Cairo Santos opened the scoring from 41, Williams flipped a 3-yard score to D'Andre Swift, and later Zavion Thomas ripped off a 30-yard run that set up a 15-yard touchdown to Colston Loveland two plays later. That made it 16-0 in the second quarter. Santos pushed the extra point wide right, which I'll be grumbling about in my sleep.

Thomas was a live wire all day. He also caught two balls for 56 yards, including a 40-yarder on third-and-17 in the third that set Santos up for a 35-yard field goal and a 19-10 lead.

Now, the defense. Jeffery Simmons had three sacks. Three! Montez Sweat dropped Tyler Shough in the end zone for a safety early in the fourth quarter, and that made it 21-10. Cam Lewis and Clark Phillips III got sacks too, six in all. Dillon Thieneman intercepted Shough, Austin Booker fell on a fumble, and when the Saints got to our 10 in the fourth, we stopped them cold on fourth-and-2.

It wasn't perfect. Williams threw an interception, Swift coughed one up in the fourth, and we went 5 for 12 on third down. Chris Olave caught nine balls for 102 yards against us, and Travis Etienne Jr. broke a 46-yarder that set up their only touchdown. Charlie Smyth also banged one in from 56 at the end of the half, and I didn't love that.

The city had a big weekend before we even got to the lakefront. Navy Pier kicked off its Winter Fireworks on Saturday night, the first of a show every Saturday through Dec. 26, and on Sunday our defensive front brought the noise. Okay, a safety isn't fireworks. It sure felt like it from where I was standing.

Short week now. We head to Ford Field to face the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 1 PM ET, and both teams are 8-2. Eat early. Bear down.

articles.title: New Orleans Saints vs Chicago Bears Week 11: Sacked Six Times, 13-21
articles.matchup: Final: Chicago Bears (8-2) 21, New Orleans Saints (3-7) 13, Sun., Nov. 22, Soldier Field, Chicago. Next: at Cincinnati Bengals, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Paycor Stadium, Cincinnati
articles.text:
Chicago 21, New Orleans 13, and my throat is raw from yelling at the screen. We're 3-7. Tyler Shough got sacked six times at Soldier Field, once in our own end zone for a safety, and you can't win on the road when your quarterback spends half the afternoon looking at the sky.

The first half got away from us fast. A short completion to CJ Donaldson turned into a fumble the Bears fell on, and a few plays later we were down 10-0. Then Dillon Thieneman intercepted Shough, and Chicago needed three plays to turn that into a 16-0 lead.

Then we woke up. Shough hit Chris Olave for 24, Travis Etienne Jr. broke a 46-yard run to the Chicago 4, and on fourth-and-goal from the 1, Shough flipped it to Alvin Kamara for the touchdown. 16-7. Danny Stutsman intercepted Caleb Williams on the very next snap. Charlie Smyth missed from 47 on that drive, but he got another crack before halftime and nailed a 56-yarder as the clock hit zero. 16-10 at the break. We were in it.

The second half was a grind, and we lost the grind. Jeffery Simmons sacked Shough three times on the day. Early in the fourth, Montez Sweat dropped him in the end zone, and it was 21-10. Julian Blackmon jumped on a D'Andre Swift fumble right after that, and we drove all the way to the Chicago 10 before coming up empty on fourth-and-2. That one stung the worst.

Smyth hit from 51 with 1:10 left, and that was the last of it. Shough finished 25 of 42 for 222 yards and ran for 34 more. Olave caught nine balls for 102 yards, Devaughn Vele had seven for 76, and Etienne ran for 76. Stutsman led us with nine tackles, Jonas Sanker had seven and a sack, and Colby Wooden got to Williams too. Good fight. Not enough.

Back home on Sunday, the Nine Times Social Aid and Pleasure Club paraded through the Ninth Ward from noon to 4 with music and dancing, up Higgins Boulevard and across St. Claude Avenue. Those folks danced for four straight hours. Our offense danced for about seven minutes in the second quarter. I know which crew I'd rather follow down the street.

Next up: the Saints go to Paycor Stadium to face the Cincinnati Bengals, Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 PM ET. Protect the quarterback. That's the whole list. Who Dat.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills vs Miami Dolphins Week 11: Bass Boots Four, 26-9
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bills (9-1) 26, Miami Dolphins (1-9) 9, Sun., Nov. 22, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park. Next: vs Kansas City Chiefs, Thu., Nov. 26, 8:20 PM ET, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park
articles.text:
Bills 26, Dolphins 9, and we're 9-1 with a short week and the Chiefs coming to town. That's the headline. The fine print says it took four Tyler Bass field goals and a defense that never let Miami sniff the end zone.

Let's be honest about the offense first. Josh Allen threw for 304 yards and a touchdown, but he also threw two interceptions, both in the final two minutes of the first half, and one of them handed Miami a field goal. We went 2 for 5 in the red zone. Against a 1-9 team, that's how you let a game hang around.

Still, the good stuff was really good. Khalil Shakir caught five balls for 101 yards, including a 38-yarder on the third-quarter drive that ended with Bass hitting from 40. DJ Moore had eight catches for 91 yards and caught the 4-yard touchdown that made it 13-0 early in the second quarter. James Cook III carried 22 times for 89 yards and plowed in from the 1 to make it 20-3.

Even the kicking crew got bold. Tommy Doman Jr. took a fourth-and-8 from punt formation, threw it to Keleki Latu for 30 yards, and Bass drilled a 54-yarder on that same drive. Bass missed from 54 in the third, but he went 4 for 5, and I won't complain about a guy who hit from 43 and 54 in the first quarter alone.

The defense was the real story. Miami went 2 for 14 on third down and gained 185 yards all day. Greg Rousseau had two sacks and kept Kyle McCord running for his life. Damar Hamlin came up with an interception. Davison Igbinosun broke up two throws, and twice in the fourth quarter Miami came up empty on fourth down in our end.

And how about this weather? Western New York got a warm weekend in late November, a high near 64 on Saturday with the same forecast for Sunday, according to the National Weather Service outlook. Sixty-four degrees in Orchard Park the week before Thanksgiving. I wore a hoodie to the game and felt like a tourist.

Now it gets real. The Kansas City Chiefs come to Highmark Stadium on Thanksgiving night, Thursday, Nov. 26, at 8:20 PM ET. Four days to fix the giveaways. Let's go Buffalo.

articles.title: Miami Dolphins vs Buffalo Bills Week 11: Nine Points, All Leg, 9-26
articles.matchup: Final: Buffalo Bills (9-1) 26, Miami Dolphins (1-9) 9, Sun., Nov. 22, Highmark Stadium, Orchard Park. Next: vs New York Jets, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Hard Rock Stadium, Miami Gardens
articles.text:
Buffalo 26, Miami 9, and the only Dolphin who scored all afternoon in Orchard Park was the kicker. Daniel Carlson went 3 for 3, from 52, 52 and 27 yards, and that was our entire offense. We're 1-9, and I'm not dressing it up.

The Bills piled up 405 yards to our 185. Kyle McCord finished 12 of 33 for 102 yards with an interception, and we went 2 for 14 on third down. Two for fourteen. You can't live like that against a 9-1 team in its own building. Our one trip inside their 20 ended with Carlson kicking from 27, and in the fourth quarter we got turned away on fourth down twice.

Here's what I'm keeping. Ollie Gordon II ran like he had somewhere to be, 11 carries for 69 yards, including a 24-yard burst on our best drive of the day to open the third. Malik Washington caught three for 30 and grabbed a 21-yarder on that same march.

And the defense kept us in this way longer than the offense deserved. Jacob Rodriguez made 13 tackles and intercepted Josh Allen, then ran it back 26 yards to set up Carlson's second 52-yarder right before the half. Zayne Anderson had 12 tackles, a sack, three throws broken up and an interception of his own. Jordyn Brooks got to Allen too. Allen threw for 304 yards and still found the end zone through the air once, a 4-yarder to DJ Moore. Our guys made him earn every inch.

But Buffalo just kept kicking. Tyler Bass hit four field goals, James Cook III bulled in from a yard out, and it was 20-6 at the break. We got it to 20-9 in the third quarter and never got closer.

Back home, the Miami Book Fair wrapped its 43rd year this weekend with the Street Fair filling downtown around Miami Dade College's Wolfson Campus from Friday through Sunday. Hundreds of authors, three languages, and not one of them could have written us a happy ending in Orchard Park. Somebody down there should write a book on converting third-and-long. I'd buy ten copies.

Next up, we come home to Hard Rock Stadium to face the New York Jets, Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 PM ET. That's the team we beat for our only win back in October. Let's make it two, and let's find the end zone while we're at it.

articles.matchup: Final: New York Giants (6-3-1) 23, Jacksonville Jaguars (7-3) 18, Sun., Nov. 22, MetLife Stadium, East Rutherford. Next: at Indianapolis Colts, Sun., Nov. 29, 1:00 PM ET, Lucas Oil Stadium, Indianapolis
articles.text:
Giants 23, Jaguars 18, and Big Blue just handed a 7-3 team a long flight home. We're 6-3-1, we shook off that Thursday night mess against Washington, and I'm still wearing my free beanie at midnight.

It was Salute to Service day at MetLife Stadium, and the first 25,000 fans through the gates got a military knit beanie from Ford. I was one of them. My dad served, so I wore it the whole game, and the defense played like it knew what day it was.

Abdul Carter was a wrecking ball. Two sacks, two tackles for loss and five hits on Trevor Lawrence. DJ Reader sacked him on Jacksonville's opening drive and forced a field goal. articles.title: Denver Broncos vs Raiders Week 11: Coleman Runs Wild, 38-24
articles.matchup: Final: Denver Broncos (8-2) 38, Raiders (4-7) 24, Sun., Nov. 22, Empower Field at Mile High, Denver. Next: at Pittsburgh Steelers, Fri., Nov. 27, 3:00 PM ET, Acrisure Stadium, Pittsburgh
articles.text:
Broncos 38, Raiders 24, and Jonah Coleman just ran through Denver like he pays rent here. Three rushing touchdowns, 111 yards on 24 carries, and we're 8-2 with six straight wins and still unbeaten at Empower Field at Mile High this year. Somebody tell the rest of the AFC West.

Friday night the Mile High Tree came on at Tivoli Quad on the Auraria Campus, 110 feet tall with 60,000 LED lights. Sunday our offense put on its own light show for a half. Wil Lutz hit from 38. Bo Nix flipped a 1-yard touchdown to Adam Trautman ten seconds into the second quarter. Marvin Mims Jr. hauled in a 36-yard bomb, and Coleman punched it in from a yard out. 17-0, and the whole stadium was shaking.

Then we got sloppy, and I'm not going to pretend we didn't. The Raiders went 84 yards in 1:54 before the half, the last 68 on a throw to Ashton Jeanty that nobody laid a hand on. Nix got intercepted by Isaiah Pola-Mao in the end zone with five seconds left in the half. In the third, Nix got stuffed on fourth-and-1 at our own 39, and Fernando Mendoza turned it into a 19-yard touchdown to Ian Thomas. 17-17. My stomach dropped all the way to Colorado Springs.

Coleman answered. A 10-play, 72-yard drive ended with his 4-yard run with 20 seconds left in the third. After the Raiders came up empty on fourth down, he went in from 7 yards out to make it 31-17. Meanwhile the defense lived in Mendoza's face all day: five sacks, two from Jonathon Cooper, one each from Alex Singleton and Malcolm Roach, and a split one for Zach Allen and Nik Bonitto. Our linebacker Singleton also had 11 tackles.

And then Ja'Quan McMillian slammed the door. With 1:52 left he jumped a throw meant for Tre Tucker and took it 35 yards the other way for six. 38-24. Go home.

It wasn't pretty everywhere. Nix went 19 of 35 for 225 yards with that interception, and we gave up 370 yards. But we were perfect in the red zone, four trips and four touchdowns, and we got flagged twice all day. Evan Engram caught six balls for 74 yards, and Jaylen Waddle added 61 on three grabs.

Short week now. Thanksgiving leftovers, then a Friday afternoon trip to Pittsburgh. Bring the orange.

articles.title: Raiders vs Denver Broncos Week 11: Flags Bury Comeback, 24-38
articles.matchup: Final: Denver Broncos (8-2) 38, Raiders (4-7) 24, Sun., Nov. 22, Empower Field at Mile High, Denver. Next: at Cleveland Browns, Sun., Nov. 29, 8:20 PM ET, Huntington Bank Field, Cleveland
articles.text:
Broncos 38, Raiders 24. We crawled out of a 17-0 hole, tied it in the third quarter, and still left Empower Field at Mile High with our third straight loss and a 4-7 record. That one's going to sit in my chest all week.

Back home Saturday night, The District at Green Valley Ranch in Henderson made snow fall on Main Street for its tree lighting. Fake snow in the desert. It felt about as real as our first quarter, when we punted on our first three drives and watched Denver go up 17-0.

Fernando Mendoza kept swinging, though. Down 17-3, he hit Ashton Jeanty on a 68-yard catch-and-run touchdown with 2:45 left in the half. Jeanty was the best player on the field for us: a 46-yard run, 79 rushing yards on 11 carries, and 90 more through the air. Then Isaiah Pola-Mao intercepted Bo Nix in the end zone with five seconds left before halftime. In the third, Maxx Crosby and Folorunso Fatukasi stuffed Nix on fourth-and-1, and Mendoza found Ian Thomas from 19 yards out. 17-17. I was on my feet screaming.

Here's what buried us: flags. Nine penalties for 63 yards, and two of them erased touchdown throws to Jalen Nailor, one for offensive interference and one for an illegal forward throw. You don't get to erase your own touchdowns in Denver and win. We also went 0 for 2 on fourth down and let Mendoza get sacked five times.

Jonah Coleman scored with 20 seconds left in the third and again early in the fourth, and suddenly it was 31-17. Mendoza fought back with a 7-yard strike to Jack Bech with 4:29 to go. Then Ja'Quan McMillian jumped a throw meant for Tre Tucker and ran 35 yards for the score that ended it.

Mendoza finished 18 of 37 for 267 yards, three touchdowns and one interception. Bech caught eight balls for 88 yards. Nakobe Dean had 12 tackles and a sack, and Quay Walker had 11 tackles. The quarterback has guts. The protection has to show up next to him.

Next up: Sunday night in Cleveland against the Browns, Nov. 29. Fix the flags and we can win that one.
